round2_findings_retested.P-R2-1: RESOLVED. The blocker was that host.configure left writer_epoch absent while its payload named model_id, which internal/domain/client_protocol.go:149-155 refuses. Measured now: apps/cli/cli_v2.go:164-176 assigns env.WriterEpoch for host.configure when model_id or provider_id is present and refuses locally at ctx.epoch == 0 before building the request; host.configure is not in v2WriteMethods (apps/cli/cli_v2.go:32-34) exactly as claimed. My own decoder replay: 7/7 accepted, 0 refused (round 2: 5/5 host.configure refused). The card can now see it: M-E1 (wire assignment guarded off) dies on W0503-MODEL-CHANGE-CARRIES-THE-OBSERVED-EPOCH, W0503-SETTLED-MODEL-CHANGE-SENDS-HOST-CONFIGURE and W0503-TABLE-ROWS-ALL-PROVEN in 4/4 runs at FAIL 92, and M-E2 (local refusal guarded off) dies on W0503-MODEL-CHANGE-WITHOUT-EPOCH-REFUSES-BEFORE-THE-HOST alone in 4/4 runs at FAIL 94, so neither half can substitute for the other. Observed versus invented: an epoch supplied by --writer-epoch is INVENTED, not observed - nothing in apps/cli ever records cfg.WriterEpoch from a host answer, and my --writer-epoch 9999 envelope passed the product decoder and reached the core's write dispatcher. That does not reopen the blocker: the card's enforceable property is 'a switch always carries a non-zero epoch assertion and never lands silently', which holds. What does not hold is the source sentence claiming the core refuses a non-current epoch; see P-R3-2.

survivor_classification.R2-M3-add-host-configure-to-v2WriteMetho: MISSING COVERAGE, low severity. The card's deliberate choice (host.configure kept out of the write table) is real in the source but unasserted: adding it would make the CLI demand project_id and expected_revision on a host-level command, i.e. refuse more than the core does, so the risk direction is a spurious refusal rather than a silent acceptance. Compensating control: internal/domain/client_protocol.go:44-48 does not list host.configure either, so the mirror is anchored to the frozen core table even though no row checks it. The assertion that would close it is the same one that closes P-R2-12 - compare v2WriteMethods against the published x-method-contracts write classification.
survivor_classification.SD1-fixture-strictWrite-drops-goal-start: MISSING COVERAGE, and the direct answer to the duplication question. The strict fixture's write table (v2verbs.go:37-39) can be weakened by deleting an entry with every row green, because nothing compares strictWrite to the product's v2WriteMethods or the core's writeMethods. Classify as missing coverage of the fixture's own integrity, not a product defect.
survivor_classification.R2-M4-table-claims-a-method-the-code-nev: MISSING COVERAGE. The compensating control the builder added is real but bounded: the ledger checks a fixed six-item literal list against observed traffic, not the table's method column. Assertion to add: build the leg list from each command row's method column in the parsed commands record and require each claimed method in wireMethods, which would also catch doctor's missing host.status.
survivor_classification.R2-M5-proven-by-pointed-at-an-unrelated-: MISSING COVERAGE. tableRowsProven is a liveness test. Assertion to add: have each probe row record the verb it drove and require the verb named in a table row to appear in the phases that produced its proven_by ids.
survivor_classification.R2-M8 / R2-M9: REDUNDANT DEFENCE at the file that carries it, MISSING COVERAGE at the surface: W0503-NO-PROCESS-DELEGATION guards one of six delivered files, and the digest row guards byte equality rather than which binary ran. Both are disclosed as limitations with obligations by remediation_round1.json and re-listed as open by strict_fixture_round2b.json, so no claim is contradicted. Fix: package-wide os/exec rule with an exemption list naming the accepted coding_task.go; compare the published installed-file digest with the file the check launches.

judgement_on_the_duplicated_write_table.question: is the strict fixture a real adversary or a second copy that drifts?
judgement_on_the_duplicated_write_table.measured_for: SD2 - removing goal.start from the PRODUCT's v2WriteMethods, so the CLI stops sending expected_revision and writer_epoch for a write - died 4/4 at FAIL 92 on the strict rows. With an imported table the fixture's rule would have moved with the product's and nothing would have refused, so the builder's stated ground is demonstrated, not asserted, in the direction that matters.
judgement_on_the_duplicated_write_table.measured_against: SD1 - removing goal.start from the FIXTURE's strictWrite - survived with PASS 95, so the duplicate can be weakened in silence; and SD3 - adding host.status to strictWrite - died, but died on W0503-STATUS-COMPLETES-AGAINST-THE-STRICT-HOST, i.e. a fixture-only change is reported as a product failure. There is no equality check between the three copies (strictWrite in the fixture, v2WriteMethods in apps/cli, writeMethods in internal/domain), and schemaMatchesCLI compares only names.
judgement_on_the_duplicated_write_table.verdict: A real adversary with an unmonitored mirror. The duplication earns its keep for refusing product regressions, which is the failure mode the blocker lived in, so this is not a reason to reject. It is a reservation: the strict mode's own table is only as honest as whoever edits it, and drift weaker is invisible while drift stricter misattributes. One row - compare strictWrite, v2WriteMethods and internal/domain's writeMethods as sets - would close both halves and is inside this card's write scope for the two client copies.

verdict_scope: ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATIONS is directed at the W05-03 card increment. The round-2 blocker is closed by measurement at three independent authorities - the product's own DecodeEnvelope replaying the CLI's captured bytes, the real apps/control core accepting the envelope far enough to refuse on authorization rather than on shape, and two isolating mutants that each die on their own named row - and the check program's growth from 89 to 95 is honest: six ids added, none dropped, and the strict fixture demonstrably refuses a product regression the imported-table version could not (SD2). What I refuse is beyond this card: product acceptance of a model switch (no host.configure handler exists, P-R3-8), any formal case, any parent gate, and the two source sentences that still describe a guarantee the core does not provide (P-R3-2).
